Subject: Manager escrow forms + privileged communication plan — annual review

Team —

We need to lock down two things for the upcoming review cycle before we publish manager comms: 1) an "escrow" form managers will use when they need to record sensitive rating/context that should be held by HR (examples: compensation hold, privileged feedback, confidential performance notes) and 2) a short privileged-communication guidance for managers and ICs (what to say, what to route to HR/legal, and an audit trail).

Attached: Manager_Escrow_Form_v1.pdf and Privileged-Comms-FAQ.docx — these are first drafts. High-level asks:
- Can Legal (Morgan) validate the wording that triggers escrow vs. normal feedback? (cc'd externally)
- Monica: can you confirm the SOC2/compliance impacts (retention window, encryption, audit logs)?
- Laura/Markus: iterate on the manager-facing language — we want a short script and a one-email template managers can use when contacting affected employees.

Timing constraint: leadership wants a quiet rollout to directors on Dec 14 and org-wide comms on Jan 4. That gives us two weeks for legal/compliance/manager signoff. Please call out any blockers.

Thanks — Aditya

--
Aditya Rao

Thanks, Aditya — quick read-through notes below.

1) Manager_Escrow_Form_v1: I made inline suggestions in the doc (Drive link below). Main change: require a 1-line business justification and a discrete owner in HR for each escrowed item — avoids open-ended "notes" piling up.
2) Privileged-Comms-FAQ: tighten the language around "what to say in the moment" — managers need a two-sentence script + an escalation checkbox (HR only, manager+HR, legal review).

Timing: Dec 14 quiet rollout works. For orgwide comms Jan 4 I'd like one rehearsal with the director cohort the week of Dec 21 so we can gather Qs and update the FAQ.

Couple of compliance notes after a quick SOC2/privacy pass:
- Retention: Anything in the escrow bucket that contains PII or HR decision rationale should be retained for 3 years by default (matches our evidence retention) unless a legal hold applies.
- Access controls: escrowed items must be stored in an access-controlled folder with KMS encryption; HR should be the canonical owner.
- Audit logs: we will need an access log export for any request that results in acting on an escrowed item (e.g., a compensation change). Can the platform team produce a weekly access digest?

I've attached the SOC2-evidence-summary I pulled — it's a short table of required retention and encryption controls. Also: Kerri Holt (external consultant) is available next week to validate the control language if we want an outside attestation before rollout.

Monica

--
Monica Patel

Good notes. I've drafted a concise manager-facing email and a short redaction checklist for HR. Pasting the manager email draft below — feel free to lift into the template: 

--- Manager email draft ---
Subject: Quick update on this year's review process
Hi <Name>,
We have a small update to how we'll handle certain sensitive review items this year. If during your review you need to record privileged feedback (examples: protected accommodation needs, ongoing investigations, or legal-sensitive performance notes), please use the attached Manager Escrow Form. HR will hold these notes securely and only surface them to the relevant stakeholders. If you're unsure, select "Discuss with HR" and we'll help triage.
Thank you,
<Manager name>
--- end draft ---

Redaction checklist (HR):
- Remove direct identifiers from non-actionable notes
- Flag any material that might trigger a legal hold
- Confirm retention period (3 years standard)

Attached is Manager_Comm_Template_v2.html with the manager email template and the redaction checklist embedded. I also inserted a small FAQ snippet for managers to use in live Q&As.

Markus
